title: Audible primitive two-torus areas on a flat three-torus
exact_target: Find surface-area analogues of spectral/length relations and count minimal surfaces in prescribed flat four-torus classes.

sources.citation: ULAM.AI and the UnsolvedMath Contributors, UnsolvedMath, record 20002524 (AIM-PHYSICS-0032). Catalogue curation under CC BY 4.0; definitions and English exposition added locally.
American Institute of Mathematics, $L^2$ harmonic forms in geometry and string theory; notes by Anda Degeratu and Mark Haskins, March 2004, 18 March 2004, Cherkis area-spectrum questions.

status_qualification: The source leaves the counting convention and the relevant area-spectrum objects open; translations and continuous families cannot silently be discarded. The title’s primitive two-torus example does not replace the full three-part target. The extracted background remarks spill into separate subsequent Jardim Dirac-spectrum questions and the Hausel programme; those are not silently reassigned to this canonical three-part Cherkis excerpt. The catalogue title/status was paired with a machine-generated research attempt; that attempt is not peer-reviewed evidence of settlement. The statement covers the original source questions rather than only the title’s subcase.
